request: I need a wall-mounted clip that snaps onto a tube, a rod or pipe with a 12 mm outer diameter, i.e. a 12 mm tube. It's C-shaped, held to the wall by a pair of M3 countersunk screws set 30 mm apart, side by side across the clip. The tube enters sideways through a 10.5 mm mouth and snaps in; the arms are 2.2 mm thick. Along the tube the clip is 12 to 30 mm wide. Make it a single FDM print with the opening facing up, so the layer lines follow the direction the arms flex. Requirements: Declare a layout with the catalogue's 12 mm tube seated in the round bore of the clip, mouth upward, and the two M3 countersunk screws sitting in the wall holes, with no parts colliding. The 12 mm tube sits in a round bore with a slight all-round gap of 0.05 to 0.15 mm on each side. Because the clip encloses over half of the tube, the only way out, crosswise to its axis, is the mouth. With a mouth opening of 10.5 mm, the tube must press in along the mouth direction and contact only the two lips on the way through. The lips' end faces form a lead-in, sloping between 20 and 60 degrees from horizontal. Make the two arms 2.2 mm thick and free to flex, long enough that spreading by the 0.75 mm per side the tube needs keeps bending strain at or below 3 %. In the worst tolerance case, a 12.1 mm tube and a mouth 0.1 mm smaller, strain must stay within 3.5 %. The clip is fixed to the wall with a pair of M3 countersunk screws spaced exactly 30 mm apart. The countersinks must leave each head flush or below the clip's surface, and every hole needs 1.5 mm or more of surrounding material on a flange that is 3 to 4 mm thick. Nothing may stick out below the flat wall face of the clip, and with the tube fitted a screwdriver must still get to every screw. The clip is printed as a single manifold body with no supports, wall face on the bed and the mouth pointing up, so the arms flex within the plane of the layers. The clip must fit inside 50 x 30 x 20 mm. Supply the STL of the clip, its OpenSCAD source, the layout declaration and the agent's own clearance report, which has to match an independent measurement.
